title: Products of pro-étale module sheaves are exact
statement:
Let $\mathcal R$ be a sheaf of rings on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$. For every set $I$ and every
family of short exact sequences $0\to A_i\to B_i\to C_i\to0$ of $\mathcal R$-modules,
the sequence $0\to\prod_iA_i\to\prod_iB_i\to\prod_iC_i\to0$ is exact. Equivalently, the
functor $\prod_{i\in I}\colon\Mod(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal R)^I\to
\Mod(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal R)$ is exact.

proof.text: Let L be the discrete-I limit functor on module sheaves. It is additive because it preserves binary products. To prove that L preserves finite colimits it suffices, by Mathlib Functor.exact_tfae, to prove that it preserves exact short complexes. Fix an exact short complex S of I-indexed module-sheaf diagrams and an affine weakly contractible W. By det-pe-sections-limits-colimits, evaluation E at W preserves finite limits and finite colimits. Whiskering diagrams with E is therefore exact, so S remains exact after evaluation. Mathlib ModuleCat.AB supplies exact products of modules; transport its instance from ULift I to I along the discrete equivalence to account for the coefficient and index universes. Applying the module limit functor gives an exact short complex.

proof.text: The natural isomorphism preservesLimitNatIso E identifies the evaluated sheaf-limit short complex with the module-limit short complex just shown exact. Transport exactness along the induced short-complex isomorphism. Apply the first clause of det-pe-sections-conservative to conclude exactness of S.map L. Functor.exact_tfae now gives finite-colimit preservation by L, which is HasExactLimitsOfShape (Discrete I). This also proves endpoint exactness: preservation of all exact short complexes implies preservation of short exact complexes, by applying exactness to zero-endpoint complexes as in Mathlib exact_tfae. The argument includes empty I.
